title: Quantifying the contribution of protein–calcium complexes to irreversible membrane fouling in casein whey ultrafiltration

record.title: Quantifying the contribution of protein–calcium complexes to irreversible membrane fouling in casein whey ultrafiltration
record.abstract: The role of calcium–protein interactions in irreversible fouling was investigated during ultrafiltration of model casein whey streams at calcium concentrations of 0, 1, 2, and 4 mM (as CaCl₂) at pH 6.2 and 7.0 using 10 kDa polyethersulphone membranes. Complexation of calcium with β-casein fragments and soluble caseins was monitored by inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES) of permeate fractions. Irreversible fouling resistance increased linearly with calcium concentration at pH 6.2, reaching 5.9 × 10¹² m⁻¹ at 4 mM Ca²⁺, versus a near-independent response at pH 7.0 (2.1–2.6 × 10¹² m⁻¹). A 0.2% citric acid pre-rinse prior to NaOH CIP improved irreversible resistance removal by 34% under high-calcium conditions. ICP-OES profiling of the cleaned membrane surface confirmed calcium persistence after alkaline-only cleaning. The findings support inclusion of an acidic chelating rinse step in CIP protocols for casein whey processing lines.
